section_1.title: The Perspective Problem: Two Maps, One Forest
section_1.content: Introduce the concept that coordinates are not absolute; they depend on the 'basis' or perspective chosen. We begin with a scenario where two characters describe the same location differently.
section_1.example: A Human uses a standard North-East grid (Standard Basis), while an Owl perched on a tilted branch uses the direction of the branch and its perpendicular as her grid. A mouse at point (3,2) for the Human is at a completely different coordinate for the Owl.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Check: What is a Basis?
section_2.content: Briefly define a basis as a set of linearly independent vectors that span the space. Visually represent the 'Standard Basis' (i, j) as a rigid square grid.
section_2.example: Show the vector v = 2i + 3j. Explain that the numbers (2, 3) are just 'instructions' (2 steps right, 3 steps up) relative to the grid lines.

section_3.title: The 'Dictionary': The Transition Matrix
section_3.content: Explain that to translate between the Human and the Owl, we need a 'dictionary.' This dictionary is the Transition Matrix (P). It is built by expressing the Owl's basis vectors in terms of the Human's coordinates.
section_3.example: If the Owl's first unit vector looks like (1, 1) to the Human and her second looks like (-1, 1), these vectors become the columns of our Transition Matrix P.

section_4.title: The Mathematical Transformation
section_4.content: Introduce the formula: [x]basis_A = P * [x]basis_B. Show how multiplying the Owl's coordinates by the matrix 'warps' her tilted grid back into the Human's standard grid.
section_4.example: Animate the Owl's tilted grid lines stretching and rotating until they align with the Human's square grid. If the Owl sees a point at (1, 1), the matrix multiplication reveals the Human sees it at (0, 2).

section_5.title: The Inverse Journey: Going Back
section_5.content: Discuss how to go from the Standard Basis to the New Basis using the inverse matrix (P⁻¹). This emphasizes that change of basis is a two-way street.
section_5.example: The Human wants to tell the Owl where a tasty snack is. He takes his coordinates, applies the inverse matrix P⁻¹, and gives the Owl instructions that match her tilted world.

section_6.title: Summary and Real-World Utility
section_6.content: Recap the core idea: Change of basis doesn't move the point; it just changes the language we use to describe its location. Mention applications like image compression (JPEG) or facial recognition (Eigenfaces).
section_6.example: In computer graphics, a character's arm has its own basis. When the arm moves, we change the basis to relate the 'hand coordinates' back to the 'body coordinates' to render the image correctly.

section_1.title: The Perspective Problem: Two Maps, One Forest
section_1.content: Introduce the concept that coordinates are not absolute; they depend on the 'basis' or perspective chosen. We begin with a scenario where two characters describe the same location differently.
section_1.example: A Human uses a standard North-East grid (Standard Basis), while an Owl perched on a tilted branch uses the direction of the branch and its perpendicular as her grid. A mouse at point (3,2) for the Human is at a completely different coordinate for the Owl.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Check: What is a Basis?
section_2.content: Briefly define a basis as a set of linearly independent vectors that span the space. Visually represent the 'Standard Basis' (i, j) as a rigid square grid.
section_2.example: Show the vector v = 2i + 3j. Explain that the numbers (2, 3) are just 'instructions' (2 steps right, 3 steps up) relative to the grid lines.

section_3.title: The 'Dictionary': The Transition Matrix
section_3.content: Explain that to translate between the Human and the Owl, we need a 'dictionary.' This dictionary is the Transition Matrix (P). It is built by expressing the Owl's basis vectors in terms of the Human's coordinates.
section_3.example: If the Owl's first unit vector looks like (1, 1) to the Human and her second looks like (-1, 1), these vectors become the columns of our Transition Matrix P.

section_4.title: The Mathematical Transformation
section_4.content: Introduce the formula: [x]basis_A = P * [x]basis_B. Show how multiplying the Owl's coordinates by the matrix 'warps' her tilted grid back into the Human's standard grid.
section_4.example: Animate the Owl's tilted grid lines stretching and rotating until they align with the Human's square grid. If the Owl sees a point at (1, 1), the matrix multiplication reveals the Human sees it at (0, 2).

section_5.title: The Inverse Journey: Going Back
section_5.content: Discuss how to go from the Standard Basis to the New Basis using the inverse matrix (P⁻¹). This emphasizes that change of basis is a two-way street.
section_5.example: The Human wants to tell the Owl where a tasty snack is. He takes his coordinates, applies the inverse matrix P⁻¹, and gives the Owl instructions that match her tilted world.

section_6.title: Summary and Real-World Utility
section_6.content: Recap the core idea: Change of basis doesn't move the point; it just changes the language we use to describe its location. Mention applications like image compression (JPEG) or facial recognition (Eigenfaces).
section_6.example: In computer graphics, a character's arm has its own basis. When the arm moves, we change the basis to relate the 'hand coordinates' back to the 'body coordinates' to render the image correctly.

outline.title: Summary and Real-World Utility
outline.content: Recap the core idea: Change of basis doesn't move the point; it just changes the language we use to describe its location. Mention applications like image compression (JPEG) or facial recognition (Eigenfaces).
outline.example: In computer graphics, a character's arm has its own basis. When the arm moves, we change the basis to relate the 'hand coordinates' back to the 'body coordinates' to render the image correctly.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Coordinates depend on your chosen perspective or basis.",
            "Meet the Human, using a standard North-East grid.",
            "Meet the Owl, using her tilted branch as reference.",
            "A mouse's location looks different to each observer.",
            "Same physical point, but two different sets of coordinates."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Perspective Problem: Two Maps, One Forest", lecture_lines)

        # Colors for reference
        STANDARD_COLOR = BLUE_B
        OWL_COLOR = YELLOW_B
        MOUSE_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        HIGHLIGHT_BLUE = "#0000FF"
        HIGHLIGHT_YELLOW = "#FFFF00"
        TEXT_COLOR = WHITE

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(STANDARD_COLOR)
        
        human_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1], y_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": STANDARD_COLOR, "stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        )
        owl_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1], y_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": OWL_COLOR, "stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        ).rotate(30 * DEGREES)
        
        grid_group = VGroup(human_grid, owl_grid)
        self.place_in_area(grid_group, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(Create(human_grid), Create(owl_grid), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(STANDARD_COLOR)
        
        mouse_pos = human_grid.c2p(3, 2)
        mouse_icon = Dot(mouse_pos, color=MOUSE_COLOR, radius=0.1)
        mouse_label = MathTex("(3, 2)", color=MOUSE_COLOR, font_size=28).next_to(mouse_icon, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        human_label = Text("Human's Grid", color=STANDARD_COLOR, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(human_label, "A3", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(FadeIn(mouse_icon), Write(mouse_label), FadeIn(human_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(OWL_COLOR)
        
        owl_label = Text("Owl's Grid", color=OWL_COLOR, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(owl_label, "A5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Human unit vectors
        i_vec = Arrow(human_grid.c2p(0,0), human_grid.c2p(1,0), color=HIGHLIGHT_BLUE, buff=0, stroke_width=6)
        j_vec = Arrow(human_grid.c2p(0,0), human_grid.c2p(0,1), color=HIGHLIGHT_BLUE, buff=0, stroke_width=6)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(owl_label))
        self.play(Indicate(i_vec), Indicate(j_vec))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(MOUSE_COLOR)
        
        # Owl basis vectors (rotated)
        u1_vec = Arrow(owl_grid.c2p(0,0), owl_grid.c2p(1,0), color=HIGHLIGHT_YELLOW, buff=0, stroke_width=6)
        u2_vec = Arrow(owl_grid.c2p(0,0), owl_grid.c2p(0,1), color=HIGHLIGHT_YELLOW, buff=0, stroke_width=6)
        
        self.play(Indicate(u1_vec), Indicate(u2_vec))
        
        # Coordinate calculation for (3,2) in 30-deg rotated basis:
        # P_owl = R^T * P_human
        # P_owl = [[cos 30, sin 30], [-sin 30, cos 30]] * [3, 2] = [3.6, 0.23]
        owl_coords_text = MathTex("(3.60, 0.23)_{Owl}", color=OWL_COLOR, font_size=28).next_to(mouse_icon, DR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Write(owl_coords_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(TEXT_COLOR)
        
        info_text = Text("One Point, Two Descriptions", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(info_text, "F3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            mouse_icon.animate.scale(2),
            Write(info_text)
        )
        self.wait(2)

                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

            "- These Human-relative vectors become the matrix columns.",
            "- Each column translates one basis vector's language.",
            "- This matrix acts as our mathematical dictionary."
        ])

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("The Inverse Journey: Going Back", [
            "- Use the inverse matrix to return to the original basis.",
            "- Change of basis is a two-way mathematical street.",
            "- The Human translates his coordinates for the Owl's world."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the inverse formula '[x]_Owl = P^-1 * [x]_Human' in #FFFFFF.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        formula = MathTex(
            r"[\mathbf{x}]_{\text{Owl}} = P^{-1} [\mathbf{x}]_{\text{Human}}",
            color="#FFFFFF"
        )
        # Position formula at the top of the workspace
        self.place_in_area(formula, "A2", "A5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show a static point on the standard grid and highlight its coordinates.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Grid plane: Human's standard basis (Identity)
        # Centered in the right area
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_numbers": False},
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": "#4444FF", "stroke_opacity": 0.5}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, "C2", "F5")
        
        # Absolute point in the standard basis (the snack)
        point_coords = [1, 1]
        dot = Dot(plane.c2p(*point_coords), color="#FF0000")
        
        human_coord_label = MathTex(
            r"[\mathbf{x}]_{\text{Human}} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}",
            color="#FF0000", font_size=28
        )
        # Position label above the left side of the grid
        self.place_at_grid(human_coord_label, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(plane))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot), Write(human_coord_label))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Animate the standard grid warping into the Owl's tilted grid #FFFF00.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Define transformation matrix P (Owl basis in Human coordinates)
        # Choosing a specific basis for visualization: b1=[1, 0.5], b2=[0.5, 1]
        matrix_P = [[1, 0.5], [0.5, 1]]
        
        # Owl coordinate label
        # Calculation: [x]_Owl = P^-1 * [1, 1] = [2/3, 2/3]
        owl_coord_label = MathTex(
            r"[\mathbf{x}]_{\text{Owl}} = \begin{bmatrix} 2/3 \\ 2/3 \end{bmatrix}",
            color="#FFFF00", font_size=28
        )
        # Position label above the right side of the grid
        self.place_at_grid(owl_coord_label, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Warp the grid by matrix P. 
        # The dot stays at the same world position [1, 1].
        self.play(
            plane.animate.apply_matrix(matrix_P).set_color("#FFFF00"),
            human_coord_label.animate.set_opacity(0.4),
            run_time=3
        )
        
        self.play(Write(owl_coord_label))
        self.wait(3)
        
        # Cleanup and finalize
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(2)

        # Cleanup and finalize
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The 'Dictionary': The Transition Matrix
outline.content: Explain that to translate between the Human and the Owl, we need a 'dictionary.' This dictionary is the Transition Matrix (P). It is built by expressing the Owl's basis vectors in terms of the Human's coordinates.
outline.example: If the Owl's first unit vector looks like (1, 1) to the Human and her second looks like (-1, 1), these vectors become the columns of our Transition Matrix P.

storyboard.title: The 'Dictionary': The Transition Matrix
lecture_lines: A transition matrix translates between different bases.
Describe the Owl's basis vectors using Human coordinates.
These Human-relative vectors become the matrix columns.
Each column translates one basis vector's language.
This matrix acts as our mathematical dictionary.
animations: Display Owl [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/owl.svg]'s basis vectors b1=(1,1) and b2=(-1,1) in #FFFF00 on the standard grid.
Animate the vector coordinates (1,1) and (-1,1) moving into a 2x2 matrix bracket.
Label the matrix 'P - Transition Matrix' in #00FFFF.
Highlight the first column of P in #FF8800 and the second column in #FF00FF.
Flash the Owl [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/owl.svg]'s basis vectors again to emphasize they are the columns of P.

outline.title: The 'Dictionary': The Transition Matrix
outline.content: Explain that to translate between the Human and the Owl, we need a 'dictionary.' This dictionary is the Transition Matrix (P). It is built by expressing the Owl's basis vectors in terms of the Human's coordinates.
outline.example: If the Owl's first unit vector looks like (1, 1) to the Human and her second looks like (-1, 1), these vectors become the columns of our Transition Matrix P.

storyboard.title: The 'Dictionary': The Transition Matrix
lecture_lines: A transition matrix translates between different bases.
Describe the Owl's basis vectors using Human coordinates.
These Human-relative vectors become the matrix columns.
Each column translates one basis vector's language.
This matrix acts as our mathematical dictionary.
animations: Display Owl [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/owl.svg]'s basis vectors b1=(1,1) and b2=(-1,1) in #FFFF00 on the standard grid.
Animate the vector coordinates (1,1) and (-1,1) moving into a 2x2 matrix bracket.
Label the matrix 'P - Transition Matrix' in #00FFFF.
Highlight the first column of P in #FF8800 and the second column in #FF00FF.
Flash the Owl [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/owl.svg]'s basis vectors again to emphasize they are the columns of P.

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with lecture lines from storyboard
        self.setup_layout("The 'Dictionary': The Transition Matrix", [
            "- A transition matrix translates between different bases.",
            "- Describe the Owl's basis vectors using Human coordinates.",
            "- These Human-relative vectors become the matrix columns.",
            "- Each column translates one basis vector's language.",
            "- This matrix acts as our mathematical dictionary."
        ])

        # Colors
        owl_color = "#FFFF00"
        matrix_label_color = "#00FFFF"
        col1_highlight = "#FF8800"
        col2_highlight = "#FF00FF"

        # Load Assets once
        owl_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/owl.svg").scale(0.4)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(owl_color))
        
        # Create coordinate plane in the grid area
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=3.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True},
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, "A2", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Owl's basis vectors: b1=(1,1) and b2=(-1,1)
        b1_arrow = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(1,1), buff=0, color=owl_color)
        b2_arrow = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(-1,1), buff=0, color=owl_color)
        
        b1_label = MathTex(r"\vec{b}_1 = (1,1)", font_size=20, color=owl_color).next_to(b1_arrow.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)
        b2_label = MathTex(r"\vec{b}_2 = (-1,1)", font_size=20, color=owl_color).next_to(b2_arrow.get_end(), UL, buff=0.1)

        # Place owl near origin
        owl_icon.move_to(plane.c2p(0,0)).shift(DOWN*0.5)

        self.play(Create(plane), GrowArrow(b1_arrow), GrowArrow(b2_arrow), FadeIn(owl_icon))
        self.play(Write(b1_label), Write(b2_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(owl_color))
        
        # Show specific coordinates for the Owl's vectors
        coord_1 = MathTex("1", "1", font_size=28, color=owl_color)
        coord_2 = MathTex("-1", "1", font_size=28, color=owl_color)
        
        self.place_at_grid(coord_1, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(coord_2, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(coord_1), Write(coord_2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(owl_color))

        # Create the transition matrix P
        matrix_p = Matrix([[1, -1], [1, 1]], h_buff=1.0, v_buff=0.7).set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_p, "D4", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        entries = matrix_p.get_entries() # Indexing: [0,0]=0, [0,1]=1, [1,0]=2, [1,1]=3
        
        # Animate coordinates moving into matrix columns
        self.play(
            FadeOut(plane), FadeOut(b1_arrow), FadeOut(b2_arrow), FadeOut(b1_label), FadeOut(b2_label), FadeOut(owl_icon),
            ReplacementTransform(coord_1[0], entries[0]),
            ReplacementTransform(coord_1[1], entries[2]),
            ReplacementTransform(coord_2[0], entries[1]),
            ReplacementTransform(coord_2[1], entries[3]),
            Write(matrix_p.get_brackets())
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(owl_color))

        # Label the matrix
        p_label = MathTex("P =", font_size=40, color=matrix_label_color).next_to(matrix_p, LEFT, buff=0.3)
        p_title = Text("Transition Matrix", font_size=24, color=matrix_label_color).next_to(matrix_p, UP, buff=0.5)
        
        self.play(Write(p_label), Write(p_title))

        # Highlight the columns
        col1_rect = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(entries[0], entries[2]), color=col1_highlight, buff=0.1)
        col2_rect = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(entries[1], entries[3]), color=col2_highlight, buff=0.1)

        self.play(Create(col1_rect))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(col1_rect, col2_rect))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(col2_rect))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(owl_color))

        # Emphasize that columns are basis vectors
        # Bring owl back
        owl_icon.scale(0.8).next_to(p_title, RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        # Show mini vectors next to matrix
        b1_mini = Arrow(ORIGIN, 0.4*(RIGHT+UP), buff=0, color=owl_color).next_to(matrix_p, LEFT, buff=1.2).shift(UP*0.3)
        b2_mini = Arrow(ORIGIN, 0.4*(LEFT+UP), buff=0, color=owl_color).next_to(matrix_p, RIGHT, buff=1.2).shift(UP*0.3)

        self.play(
            FadeIn(owl_icon),
            Indication(VGroup(entries[0], entries[2]), color=col1_highlight),
            Indication(VGroup(entries[1], entries[3]), color=col2_highlight),
            Create(b1_mini), Create(b2_mini)
        )
        
        self.play(Flash(b1_mini, color=col1_highlight), Flash(b2_mini, color=col2_highlight))

        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(b1_mini), FadeOut(b2_mini), FadeOut(owl_icon), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with lecture lines from storyboard
        self.setup_layout("The 'Dictionary': The Transition Matrix", [
            "- A transition matrix translates between different bases.",
            "- Describe the Owl's basis vectors using Human coordinates.",
            "- These Human-relative vectors become the matrix columns.",
            "- Each column translates one basis vector's language.",
            "- This matrix acts as our mathematical dictionary."
        ])

        # Colors
        owl_color = "#FFFF00"
        matrix_label_color = "#00FFFF"
        col1_highlight = "#FF8800"
        col2_highlight = "#FF00FF"

        # Load Assets once
        owl_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/owl.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(owl_icon, "E2", scale_factor=0.4)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(owl_color))
        
        # Create coordinate plane in the grid area
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=3.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True},
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, "A2", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Owl's basis vectors: b1=(1,1) and b2=(-1,1)
        b1_arrow = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(1,1), buff=0, color=owl_color)
        b2_arrow = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(-1,1), buff=0, color=owl_color)
        
        b1_label = MathTex(r"\vec{b}_1 = (1,1)", font_size=20, color=owl_color)
        b2_label = MathTex(r"\vec{b}_2 = (-1,1)", font_size=20, color=owl_color)
        
        self.place_at_grid(b1_label, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(b2_label, "B3", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(Create(plane), GrowArrow(b1_arrow), GrowArrow(b2_arrow), FadeIn(owl_icon))
        self.play(Write(b1_label), Write(b2_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(owl_color))
        
        # Show specific coordinates for the Owl's vectors
        coord_1 = VGroup(MathTex("1", font_size=32, color=owl_color), MathTex("1", font_size=32, color=owl_color)).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
        coord_2 = VGroup(MathTex("-1", font_size=32, color=owl_color), MathTex("1", font_size=32, color=owl_color)).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        self.place_at_grid(coord_1, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(coord_2, "B6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(coord_1), Write(coord_2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(owl_color))

        # Create the transition matrix P
        matrix_p = Matrix([[1, -1], [1, 1]], h_buff=1.0, v_buff=0.7).set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_p, "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        entries = matrix_p.get_entries() # Indexing: [0,0]=0, [0,1]=1, [1,0]=2, [1,1]=3
        
        # Animate coordinates moving into matrix columns
        self.play(
            FadeOut(plane), FadeOut(b1_arrow), FadeOut(b2_arrow), FadeOut(b1_label), FadeOut(b2_label), FadeOut(owl_icon),
            ReplacementTransform(coord_1[0], entries[0]),
            ReplacementTransform(coord_1[1], entries[2]),
            ReplacementTransform(coord_2[0], entries[1]),
            ReplacementTransform(coord_2[1], entries[3]),
            Write(matrix_p.get_brackets())
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(owl_color))

        # Label the matrix
        p_label = MathTex("P =", font_size=32, color=matrix_label_color)
        p_title = Text("Transition Matrix", font_size=20, color=matrix_label_color)
        
        self.place_at_grid(p_label, "D2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(p_title, "C4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(p_label), Write(p_title))

        # Highlight the columns
        col1_rect = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(entries[0], entries[2]), color=col1_highlight, buff=0.1)
        col2_rect = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(entries[1], entries[3]), color=col2_highlight, buff=0.1)

        self.play(Create(col1_rect))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(col1_rect, col2_rect))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(col2_rect))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(owl_color))

        # Emphasize that columns are basis vectors
        # Reposition owl
        self.place_at_grid(owl_icon, "C5", scale_factor=0.4)
        
        # Show mini vectors next to matrix
        b1_mini = Arrow(ORIGIN, 0.4*(RIGHT+UP), buff=0, color=owl_color)
        b2_mini = Arrow(ORIGIN, 0.4*(LEFT+UP), buff=0, color=owl_color)
        
        self.place_at_grid(b1_mini, "E3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(b2_mini, "E5", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(
            FadeIn(owl_icon),
            Indicate(VGroup(entries[0], entries[2]), color=col1_highlight),
            Indicate(VGroup(entries[1], entries[3]), color=col2_highlight),
            Create(b1_mini), Create(b2_mini)
        )
        
        self.play(Flash(b1_mini, color=col1_highlight), Flash(b2_mini, color=col2_highlight))

        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(b1_mini), FadeOut(b2_mini), FadeOut(owl_icon), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

section_1.title: The Perspective Problem: Two Maps, One Forest
section_1.content: Introduce the concept that coordinates are not absolute; they depend on the 'basis' or perspective chosen. We begin with a scenario where two characters describe the same location differently.
section_1.example: A Human uses a standard North-East grid (Standard Basis), while an Owl perched on a tilted branch uses the direction of the branch and its perpendicular as her grid. A mouse at point (3,2) for the Human is at a completely different coordinate for the Owl.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Check: What is a Basis?
section_2.content: Briefly define a basis as a set of linearly independent vectors that span the space. Visually represent the 'Standard Basis' (i, j) as a rigid square grid.
section_2.example: Show the vector v = 2i + 3j. Explain that the numbers (2, 3) are just 'instructions' (2 steps right, 3 steps up) relative to the grid lines.

section_3.title: The 'Dictionary': The Transition Matrix
section_3.content: Explain that to translate between the Human and the Owl, we need a 'dictionary.' This dictionary is the Transition Matrix (P). It is built by expressing the Owl's basis vectors in terms of the Human's coordinates.
section_3.example: If the Owl's first unit vector looks like (1, 1) to the Human and her second looks like (-1, 1), these vectors become the columns of our Transition Matrix P.

section_4.title: The Mathematical Transformation
section_4.content: Introduce the formula: [x]basis_A = P * [x]basis_B. Show how multiplying the Owl's coordinates by the matrix 'warps' her tilted grid back into the Human's standard grid.
section_4.example: Animate the Owl's tilted grid lines stretching and rotating until they align with the Human's square grid. If the Owl sees a point at (1, 1), the matrix multiplication reveals the Human sees it at (0, 2).

section_5.title: The Inverse Journey: Going Back
section_5.content: Discuss how to go from the Standard Basis to the New Basis using the inverse matrix (P⁻¹). This emphasizes that change of basis is a two-way street.
section_5.example: The Human wants to tell the Owl where a tasty snack is. He takes his coordinates, applies the inverse matrix P⁻¹, and gives the Owl instructions that match her tilted world.

section_6.title: Summary and Real-World Utility
section_6.content: Recap the core idea: Change of basis doesn't move the point; it just changes the language we use to describe its location. Mention applications like image compression (JPEG) or facial recognition (Eigenfaces).
section_6.example: In computer graphics, a character's arm has its own basis. When the arm moves, we change the basis to relate the 'hand coordinates' back to the 'body coordinates' to render the image correctly.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Check: What is a Basis?", [
            "A basis is a set of independent spanning vectors.",
            "The standard basis uses unit vectors i and j.",
            "This creates a familiar, rigid square grid.",
            "Vector v is just instructions relative to this grid.",
            "Change the basis, and you change the instructions."
        ])
        
        # Reference Origin for vectors
        origin_pt = self.grid['D3']

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show two independent vectors (not standard) and label them 'Basis B' in #00FFFF.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        v1 = Arrow(start=origin_pt, end=self.grid['C4'], color="#00FFFF", buff=0)
        v2 = Arrow(start=origin_pt, end=self.grid['B3'], color="#00FFFF", buff=0)
        basis_b_label = Text("Basis B", font_size=20, color="#00FFFF")
        basis_b_label.next_to(self.grid['B3'], UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(v1), Create(v2), Write(basis_b_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show the standard basis vectors i in #FF0000 and j in #00FF00 with labels.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF0000")
        
        i_vec = Arrow(start=origin_pt, end=self.grid['D4'], color="#FF0000", buff=0)
        j_vec = Arrow(start=origin_pt, end=self.grid['C3'], color="#00FF00", buff=0)
        i_label = MathTex("\\hat{i}", color="#FF0000", font_size=24).next_to(self.grid['D4'], DOWN, buff=0.1)
        j_label = MathTex("\\hat{j}", color="#00FF00", font_size=24).next_to(self.grid['C3'], LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(v1), FadeOut(v2), FadeOut(basis_b_label),
            Create(i_vec), Create(j_vec),
            Write(i_label), Write(j_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Draw a square grid in #444444 behind the standard basis vectors.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#888888")
        
        grid_lines = VGroup()
        for i in range(6):
            start = self.grid[f"{chr(65+i)}1"]
            end = self.grid[f"{chr(65+i)}6"]
            grid_lines.add(Line(start, end, color="#444444", stroke_width=1))
        for j in range(6):
            start = self.grid[f"A{j+1}"]
            end = self.grid[f"F{j+1}"]
            grid_lines.add(Line(start, end, color="#444444", stroke_width=1))
            
        self.play(Create(grid_lines), run_time=2)
        self.add(i_vec, j_vec, i_label, j_label)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Draw vector v = 2i + 3j in #FFFFFF; show movement 2 units right and 3 units up.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        v_target = self.grid['A5']
        v_vec = Arrow(start=origin_pt, end=v_target, color="#FFFFFF", buff=0)
        v_label = MathTex("v = [2, 3]^T", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=24).next_to(v_target, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        step_h = DashedLine(start=origin_pt, end=self.grid['D5'], color="#FFFFFF", stroke_width=2)
        step_v = DashedLine(start=self.grid['D5'], end=v_target, color="#FFFFFF", stroke_width=2)
        
        self.play(Create(step_h))
        self.play(Create(step_v))
        self.play(Create(v_vec), Write(v_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Rotate and scale the basis vectors to illustrate changing the reference instructions.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        i_new_target = self.grid['C4']
        j_new_target = self.grid['B2']
        
        self.play(
            i_vec.animate.put_start_and_end_on(origin_pt, i_new_target),
            j_vec.animate.put_start_and_end_on(origin_pt, j_new_target),
            i_label.animate.next_to(i_new_target, RIGHT, buff=0.1),
            j_label.animate.next_to(j_new_target, UP, buff=0.1),
            FadeOut(grid_lines),
            FadeOut(step_h),
            FadeOut(step_v),
            v_vec.animate.set_opacity(0.3),
            v_label.animate.set_opacity(0.3)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with lecture lines from storyboard
        self.setup_layout("The 'Dictionary': The Transition Matrix", [
            "- A transition matrix translates between different bases.",
            "- Describe the Owl's basis vectors using Human coordinates.",
            "- These Human-relative vectors become the matrix columns.",
            "- Each column translates one basis vector's language.",
            "- This matrix acts as our mathematical dictionary."
        ])

        # Colors
        owl_color = "#FFFF00"
        matrix_label_color = "#00FFFF"
        col1_highlight = "#FF8800"
        col2_highlight = "#FF00FF"

        # Load Assets once
        owl_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/owl.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(owl_icon, "E2", scale_factor=0.4)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(owl_color))
        
        # Create coordinate plane in the grid area
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=3.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True},
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, "A2", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Owl's basis vectors: b1=(1,1) and b2=(-1,1)
        b1_arrow = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(1,1), buff=0, color=owl_color)
        b2_arrow = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(-1,1), buff=0, color=owl_color)
        
        b1_label = MathTex(r"\vec{b}_1 = (1,1)", font_size=20, color=owl_color)
        b2_label = MathTex(r"\vec{b}_2 = (-1,1)", font_size=20, color=owl_color)
        
        self.place_at_grid(b1_label, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(b2_label, "B3", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(Create(plane), GrowArrow(b1_arrow), GrowArrow(b2_arrow), FadeIn(owl_icon))
        self.play(Write(b1_label), Write(b2_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(owl_color))
        
        # Show specific coordinates for the Owl's vectors
        coord_1 = VGroup(MathTex("1", font_size=32, color=owl_color), MathTex("1", font_size=32, color=owl_color)).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
        coord_2 = VGroup(MathTex("-1", font_size=32, color=owl_color), MathTex("1", font_size=32, color=owl_color)).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        self.place_at_grid(coord_1, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(coord_2, "B6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(coord_1), Write(coord_2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(owl_color))

        # Create the transition matrix P
        matrix_p = Matrix([[1, -1], [1, 1]], h_buff=1.0, v_buff=0.7).set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_p, "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        entries = matrix_p.get_entries() # Indexing: [0,0]=0, [0,1]=1, [1,0]=2, [1,1]=3
        
        # Animate coordinates moving into matrix columns
        self.play(
            FadeOut(plane), FadeOut(b1_arrow), FadeOut(b2_arrow), FadeOut(b1_label), FadeOut(b2_label), FadeOut(owl_icon),
            ReplacementTransform(coord_1[0], entries[0]),
            ReplacementTransform(coord_1[1], entries[2]),
            ReplacementTransform(coord_2[0], entries[1]),
            ReplacementTransform(coord_2[1], entries[3]),
            Write(matrix_p.get_brackets())
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(owl_color))

        # Label the matrix
        p_label = MathTex("P =", font_size=32, color=matrix_label_color)
        p_title = Text("Transition Matrix", font_size=20, color=matrix_label_color)
        
        self.place_at_grid(p_label, "D2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(p_title, "C4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(p_label), Write(p_title))

        # Highlight the columns
        col1_rect = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(entries[0], entries[2]), color=col1_highlight, buff=0.1)
        col2_rect = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(entries[1], entries[3]), color=col2_highlight, buff=0.1)

        self.play(Create(col1_rect))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(col1_rect, col2_rect))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(col2_rect))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(owl_color))

        # Emphasize that columns are basis vectors
        # Reposition owl
        self.place_at_grid(owl_icon, "C5", scale_factor=0.4)
        
        # Show mini vectors next to matrix
        b1_mini = Arrow(ORIGIN, 0.4*(RIGHT+UP), buff=0, color=owl_color)
        b2_mini = Arrow(ORIGIN, 0.4*(LEFT+UP), buff=0, color=owl_color)
        
        self.place_at_grid(b1_mini, "E3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(b2_mini, "E5", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(
            FadeIn(owl_icon),
            Indicate(VGroup(entries[0], entries[2]), color=col1_highlight),
            Indicate(VGroup(entries[1], entries[3]), color=col2_highlight),
            Create(b1_mini), Create(b2_mini)
        )
        
        self.play(Flash(b1_mini, color=col1_highlight), Flash(b2_mini, color=col2_highlight))

        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(b1_mini), FadeOut(b2_mini), FadeOut(owl_icon), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Coordinates depend on your chosen perspective or basis.",
            "Meet the Human, using a standard North-East grid.",
            "Meet the Owl, using her tilted branch as reference.",
            "A mouse's location looks different to each observer.",
            "Same physical point, but two different sets of coordinates."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Perspective Problem: Two Maps, One Forest", lecture_lines)

        # Colors for reference
        STANDARD_COLOR = BLUE_B
        OWL_COLOR = YELLOW_B
        MOUSE_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        HIGHLIGHT_BLUE = "#0000FF"
        HIGHLIGHT_YELLOW = "#FFFF00"
        TEXT_COLOR = WHITE

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(STANDARD_COLOR)
        
        human_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1], y_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": STANDARD_COLOR, "stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        )
        owl_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1], y_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": OWL_COLOR, "stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        ).rotate(30 * DEGREES)
        
        grid_group = VGroup(human_grid, owl_grid)
        self.place_in_area(grid_group, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(Create(human_grid), Create(owl_grid), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(STANDARD_COLOR)
        
        mouse_pos = human_grid.c2p(3, 2)
        mouse_icon = Dot(mouse_pos, color=MOUSE_COLOR, radius=0.1)
        mouse_label = MathTex("(3, 2)", color=MOUSE_COLOR, font_size=28).next_to(mouse_icon, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        human_label = Text("Human's Grid", color=STANDARD_COLOR, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(human_label, "A3", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(FadeIn(mouse_icon), Write(mouse_label), FadeIn(human_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(OWL_COLOR)
        
        owl_label = Text("Owl's Grid", color=OWL_COLOR, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(owl_label, "A5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Human unit vectors
        i_vec = Arrow(human_grid.c2p(0,0), human_grid.c2p(1,0), color=HIGHLIGHT_BLUE, buff=0, stroke_width=6)
        j_vec = Arrow(human_grid.c2p(0,0), human_grid.c2p(0,1), color=HIGHLIGHT_BLUE, buff=0, stroke_width=6)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(owl_label))
        self.play(Indicate(i_vec), Indicate(j_vec))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(MOUSE_COLOR)
        
        # Owl basis vectors (rotated)
        u1_vec = Arrow(owl_grid.c2p(0,0), owl_grid.c2p(1,0), color=HIGHLIGHT_YELLOW, buff=0, stroke_width=6)
        u2_vec = Arrow(owl_grid.c2p(0,0), owl_grid.c2p(0,1), color=HIGHLIGHT_YELLOW, buff=0, stroke_width=6)
        
        self.play(Indicate(u1_vec), Indicate(u2_vec))
        
        # Coordinate calculation for (3,2) in 30-deg rotated basis:
        # P_owl = R^T * P_human
        # P_owl = [[cos 30, sin 30], [-sin 30, cos 30]] * [3, 2] = [3.6, 0.23]
        owl_coords_text = MathTex("(3.60, 0.23)_{Owl}", color=OWL_COLOR, font_size=28).next_to(mouse_icon, DR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Write(owl_coords_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(TEXT_COLOR)
        
        info_text = Text("One Point, Two Descriptions", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(info_text, "F3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            mouse_icon.animate.scale(2),
            Write(info_text)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Real-World Utility", [
            "Changing the basis doesn't move the physical point.",
            "It simply changes the language used to describe location.",
            "Essential for JPEG compression and computer graphics."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Color change for line 1
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Point labeled 'Fixed Location'
        point = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(point, "C3", scale_factor=1.5)
        label_fixed = Text("Fixed Location", font_size=18, color=YELLOW)
        label_fixed.next_to(point, UP, buff=0.2)
        
        # Two sets of coordinates in standard and custom basis
        # Standard Basis Matrix E
        val_ae_x = DecimalNumber(0.0, color=BLUE, num_decimal_places=1)
        val_ae_y = DecimalNumber(0.0, color=BLUE, num_decimal_places=1)
        # Using \left[ and \right] to avoid compilation errors with incomplete environments
        bracket_l_a = MathTex(r"\left[", color=BLUE)
        bracket_r_a = MathTex(r"\right]_E", color=BLUE)
        matrix_a = VGroup(
            bracket_l_a, 
            VGroup(val_ae_x, val_ae_y).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2), 
            bracket_r_a
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Custom Basis Matrix B
        val_bb_x = DecimalNumber(0.0, color=GREEN, num_decimal_places=1)
        val_bb_y = DecimalNumber(0.0, color=GREEN, num_decimal_places=1)
        bracket_l_b = MathTex(r"\left[", color=GREEN)
        bracket_r_b = MathTex(r"\right]_B", color=GREEN)
        matrix_b = VGroup(
            bracket_l_b, 
            VGroup(val_bb_x, val_bb_y).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2), 
            bracket_r_b
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_a, "C2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_b, "C4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(point), Write(label_fixed))
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_a), FadeIn(matrix_b))
        
        # Animate coordinates "updating" to their final values simultaneously
        self.play(
            ChangeDecimalToValue(val_ae_x, 3.0),
            ChangeDecimalToValue(val_ae_y, 2.0),
            ChangeDecimalToValue(val_bb_x, 1.5),
            ChangeDecimalToValue(val_bb_y, 2.5),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transition color to line 2
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE)
        )
        
        # Pulse the matrices to emphasize "language" used to describe location
        self.play(
            matrix_a.animate.scale(1.2),
            matrix_b.animate.scale(1.2),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transition color to line 3
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF")
        )
        
        # Real-world utility descriptions
        img_comp_text = Text("Image Compression", font_size=16, color="#00FFFF")
        comp_graph_text = Text("Computer Graphics", font_size=16, color="#00FFFF")
        
        # Simple representative icons

        graphics_icon = Triangle(color="#00FFFF", fill_opacity=0.3).scale(0.3)

        icon_group_2 = VGroup(graphics_icon, comp_graph_text).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(icon_group_1, "E2")
        self.place_at_grid(icon_group_2, "E5")
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(icon_group_1, shift=UP),
            FadeIn(icon_group_2, shift=UP)
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        # === Final Summary Transition ===
        # Clear the scene and show the final overarching message
        self.play(
            FadeOut(point, label_fixed, matrix_a, matrix_b, icon_group_1, icon_group_2),
            self.lecture.animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )

        self.place_in_area(final_text, "B1", "D6")
        
        self.play(Write(final_text))
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        i_label = MathTex("\\hat{i}", color="#FF0000", font_size=24).next_to(self.grid['D4'], DOWN, buff=0.1)

        self.play(
            FadeOut(v1), FadeOut(v2), FadeOut(basis_b_label),

            Write(i_label), Write(j_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

            grid_lines.add(Line(start, end, color="#444444", stroke_width=1))

        self.add(i_vec, j_vec, i_label, j_label)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===

        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        v_target = self.grid['A5']
        v_vec = Arrow(start=origin_pt, end=v_target, color="#FFFFFF", buff=0)
        v_label = MathTex("v = [2, 3]^T", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=24).next_to(v_target, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        step_h = DashedLine(start=origin_pt, end=self.grid['D5'], color="#FFFFFF", stroke_width=2)
        step_v = DashedLine(start=self.grid['D5'], end=v_target, color="#FFFFFF", stroke_width=2)
        
        self.play(Create(step_h))
        self.play(Create(step_v))
        self.play(Create(v_vec), Write(v_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Rotate and scale the basis vectors to illustrate changing the reference instructions.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        i_new_target = self.grid['C4']
        j_new_target = self.grid['B2']
        
        self.play(
            i_vec.animate.put_start_and_end_on(origin_pt, i_new_target),
            j_vec.animate.put_start_and_end_on(origin_pt, j_new_target),
            i_label.animate.next_to(i_new_target, RIGHT, buff=0.1),
            j_label.animate.next_to(j_new_target, UP, buff=0.1),
            FadeOut(grid_lines),
            FadeOut(step_h),
            FadeOut(step_v),
            v_vec.animate.set_opacity(0.3),
            v_label.animate.set_opacity(0.3)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with lecture lines from storyboard
        self.setup_layout("The 'Dictionary': The Transition Matrix", [
            "- A transition matrix translates between different bases.",
            "- Describe the Owl's basis vectors using Human coordinates.",
            "- These Human-relative vectors become the matrix columns.",
            "- Each column translates one basis vector's language.",
            "- This matrix acts as our mathematical dictionary."
        ])

        # Colors
        owl_color = "#FFFF00"
        matrix_label_color = "#00FFFF"
        col1_highlight = "#FF8800"
        col2_highlight = "#FF00FF"

        # Load Assets once
        owl_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/owl.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(owl_icon, "E2", scale_factor=0.4)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(owl_color))
        
        # Create coordinate plane in the grid area
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=3.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True},
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, "A2", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Owl's basis vectors: b1=(1,1) and b2=(-1,1)
        b1_arrow = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(1,1), buff=0, color=owl_color)
        b2_arrow = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(-1,1), buff=0, color=owl_color)
        
        b1_label = MathTex(r"\vec{b}_1 = (1,1)", font_size=20, color=owl_color)
        b2_label = MathTex(r"\vec{b}_2 = (-1,1)", font_size=20, color=owl_color)
        
        self.place_at_grid(b1_label, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(b2_label, "B3", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(Create(plane), GrowArrow(b1_arrow), GrowArrow(b2_arrow), FadeIn(owl_icon))
        self.play(Write(b1_label), Write(b2_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(owl_color))
        
        # Show specific coordinates for the Owl's vectors
        coord_1 = VGroup(MathTex("1", font_size=32, color=owl_color), MathTex("1", font_size=32, color=owl_color)).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
        coord_2 = VGroup(MathTex("-1", font_size=32, color=owl_color), MathTex("1", font_size=32, color=owl_color)).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        self.place_at_grid(coord_1, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(coord_2, "B6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(coord_1), Write(coord_2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(owl_color))

        # Create the transition matrix P
        matrix_p = Matrix([[1, -1], [1, 1]], h_buff=1.0, v_buff=0.7).set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_p, "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        entries = matrix_p.get_entries() # Indexing: [0,0]=0, [0,1]=1, [1,0]=2, [1,1]=3
        
        # Animate coordinates moving into matrix columns
        self.play(
            FadeOut(plane), FadeOut(b1_arrow), FadeOut(b2_arrow), FadeOut(b1_label), FadeOut(b2_label), FadeOut(owl_icon),
            ReplacementTransform(coord_1[0], entries[0]),
            ReplacementTransform(coord_1[1], entries[2]),
            ReplacementTransform(coord_2[0], entries[1]),
            ReplacementTransform(coord_2[1], entries[3]),
            Write(matrix_p.get_brackets())
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(owl_color))

        # Label the matrix
        p_label = MathTex("P =", font_size=32, color=matrix_label_color)
        p_title = Text("Transition Matrix", font_size=20, color=matrix_label_color)
        
        self.place_at_grid(p_label, "D2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(p_title, "C4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(p_label), Write(p_title))

        # Highlight the columns
        col1_rect = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(entries[0], entries[2]), color=col1_highlight, buff=0.1)
        col2_rect = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(entries[1], entries[3]), color=col2_highlight, buff=0.1)

        self.play(Create(col1_rect))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(col1_rect, col2_rect))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(col2_rect))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(owl_color))

        # Emphasize that columns are basis vectors
        # Reposition owl
        self.place_at_grid(owl_icon, "C5", scale_factor=0.4)
        
        # Show mini vectors next to matrix
        b1_mini = Arrow(ORIGIN, 0.4*(RIGHT+UP), buff=0, color=owl_color)
        b2_mini = Arrow(ORIGIN, 0.4*(LEFT+UP), buff=0, color=owl_color)
        
        self.place_at_grid(b1_mini, "E3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(b2_mini, "E5", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(
            FadeIn(owl_icon),
            Indicate(VGroup(entries[0], entries[2]), color=col1_highlight),
            Indicate(VGroup(entries[1], entries[3]), color=col2_highlight),
            Create(b1_mini), Create(b2_mini)
        )
        
        self.play(Flash(b1_mini, color=col1_highlight), Flash(b2_mini, color=col2_highlight))

        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(b1_mini), FadeOut(b2_mini), FadeOut(owl_icon), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

outline.title: The Inverse Journey: Going Back
outline.content: Discuss how to go from the Standard Basis to the New Basis using the inverse matrix (P⁻¹). This emphasizes that change of basis is a two-way street.
outline.example: The Human wants to tell the Owl where a tasty snack is. He takes his coordinates, applies the inverse matrix P⁻¹, and gives the Owl instructions that match her tilted world.

storyboard.title: The Inverse Journey: Going Back
lecture_lines: Use the inverse matrix to return to the original basis.
Change of basis is a two-way mathematical street.
The Human translates his coordinates for the Owl's world.
animations: Display the inverse formula '[x]_Owl = P^-1 * [x]_Human' in #FFFFFF.
Show a static point on the standard grid and highlight its coordinates.
Animate the standard grid warping into the Owl's tilted grid #FFFF00.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("The Inverse Journey: Going Back", [
            "- Use the inverse matrix to return to the original basis.",
            "- Change of basis is a two-way mathematical street.",
            "- The Human translates his coordinates for the Owl's world."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the inverse formula '[x]_Owl = P^-1 * [x]_Human' in #FFFFFF.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        formula = MathTex(
            r"[\mathbf{x}]_{\text{Owl}} = P^{-1} [\mathbf{x}]_{\text{Human}}",
            color="#FFFFFF"
        )
        # Position formula at the top of the workspace
        self.place_in_area(formula, "A2", "A5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show a static point on the standard grid and highlight its coordinates.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Grid plane: Human's standard basis (Identity)
        # Centered in the right area
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_numbers": False},
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": "#4444FF", "stroke_opacity": 0.5}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, "C2", "F5")
        
        # Absolute point in the standard basis (the snack)
        point_coords = [1, 1]
        dot = Dot(plane.c2p(*point_coords), color="#FF0000")
        
        human_coord_label = MathTex(
            r"[\mathbf{x}]_{\text{Human}} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}",
            color="#FF0000", font_size=28
        )
        # Position label above the left side of the grid
        self.place_at_grid(human_coord_label, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(plane))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot), Write(human_coord_label))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Animate the standard grid warping into the Owl's tilted grid #FFFF00.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Define transformation matrix P (Owl basis in Human coordinates)
        # Choosing a specific basis for visualization: b1=[1, 0.5], b2=[0.5, 1]
        matrix_P = [[1, 0.5], [0.5, 1]]
        
        # Owl coordinate label
        # Calculation: [x]_Owl = P^-1 * [1, 1] = [2/3, 2/3]
        owl_coord_label = MathTex(
            r"[\mathbf{x}]_{\text{Owl}} = \begin{bmatrix} 2/3 \\ 2/3 \end{bmatrix}",
            color="#FFFF00", font_size=28
        )
        # Position label above the right side of the grid
        self.place_at_grid(owl_coord_label, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Warp the grid by matrix P. 
        # The dot stays at the same world position [1, 1].
        self.play(
            plane.animate.apply_matrix(matrix_P).set_color("#FFFF00"),
            human_coord_label.animate.set_opacity(0.4),
            run_time=3
        )
        
        self.play(Write(owl_coord_label))
        self.wait(3)
        
        # Cleanup and finalize
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(2)

        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # Storyboard: "Show a static point... Animate the standard grid warping..."

        )
        # Fix Issue 37: B6, scale 0.7
        self.place_at_grid(owl_coord_label, "B6", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # Warp the grid. Note: dot is not part of the plane VGroup in the previous step.
        # To make the grid warp while the dot stays in the same place in "world space":

        )

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("The Inverse Journey: Going Back", [
            "- Use the inverse matrix to return to the original basis.",
            "- Change of basis is a two-way mathematical street.",
            "- The Human translates his coordinates for the Owl's world."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the inverse formula '[x]_Owl = P^-1 * [x]_Human' in #FFFFFF.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        formula = MathTex(
            r"[\mathbf{x}]_{\text{Owl}} = P^{-1} [\mathbf{x}]_{\text{Human}}",
            color="#FFFFFF"
        )
        # Position formula at the top of the workspace
        # Fix Issue 38: scale_factor=0.8
        self.place_in_area(formula, "A2", "A5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show a static point on the standard grid and highlight its coordinates.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Grid plane: Human's standard basis (Identity)
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_numbers": False},
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": "#4444FF", "stroke_opacity": 0.5}
        )
        # Fix Issue 39: scale_factor=0.9
        self.place_in_area(plane, "C2", "F5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Absolute point in the standard basis (the snack)
        # Use a dot that will not be transformed by apply_matrix if added separately,
        # but here we want it to stay at the same visual position or follow the grid?
        # Storyboard: "Show a static point... Animate the standard grid warping..."
        # If the grid warps, the point (snack) remains at the same location in the world,
        # but its coordinates relative to the grid change.
        # However, apply_matrix on a plane usually transforms everything on it.
        # Let's use a Dot and keep it stationary relative to the camera to represent the "world point".
        
        world_point = [1, 1, 0]
        dot = Dot(plane.c2p(1, 1), color="#FF0000")
        
        human_coord_label = MathTex(
            r"[\mathbf{x}]_{\text{Human}} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}",
            color="#FF0000", font_size=28
        )
        # Fix Issue 37: B1, scale 0.7
        self.place_at_grid(human_coord_label, "B1", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(Create(plane))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot), Write(human_coord_label))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Animate the standard grid warping into the Owl's tilted grid #FFFF00.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Define transformation matrix P (Owl basis in Human coordinates)
        matrix_P = [[1, 0.5], [0.5, 1]]
        
        # Owl coordinate label
        owl_coord_label = MathTex(
            r"[\mathbf{x}]_{\text{Owl}} = \begin{bmatrix} 2/3 \\ 2/3 \end{bmatrix}",
            color="#FFFF00", font_size=28
        )
        # Fix Issue 37: B6, scale 0.7
        self.place_at_grid(owl_coord_label, "B6", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # Warp the grid. Note: dot is not part of the plane VGroup in the previous step.
        # To make the grid warp while the dot stays in the same place in "world space":
        # The plane's c2p(1,1) will move. We want the dot to stay at the same pixel position.
        
        self.play(
            plane.animate.apply_matrix(matrix_P).set_color("#FFFF00"),
            human_coord_label.animate.set_opacity(0.4),
            run_time=3
        )
        
        self.play(Write(owl_coord_label))
        self.wait(3)
        
        # Finalize
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(2)

### Key Updates:
- **Visual Fixes**:

  - The grid then warps into the "Owl's" tilted world using the transformation matrix $P$.
  - The resulting "Owl" coordinates $[2/3, 2/3]^T$ are displayed, demonstrating the use of the inverse matrix $P^{-1}$ to translate positions from the standard world into the specific tilted basis.

            "- The transformation reveals how the other person sees it."
        ])
        
        # Colors
        formula_white = "#FFFFFF"
        matrix_cyan = "#00FFFF"
        owl_yellow = "#FFFF00"
        point_green = "#00FF00"

        )
        self.place_in_area(context_owl_grid, 'B2', 'F6', scale_factor=1.0)
